mismatches.item: How ElevenLabs Sources Top Designers with AI
mismatches.digest_line: 30,000 inbound applications produced one design hire, so ElevenLabs sourced 60% of a team that grew from 8 to 35.
mismatches.source_says: Transcript [0:58]: "in the last year we scaled the team from eight designers to 35. 60% of those people are sourced candidates. The remaining is basically referrals". Episode description: "ElevenLabs grew its design team from 8 to 35 in a year, and 60% of those hires were sourced." The 60% is of the hires made in the year, not of the 35 person team (which includes the original 8).
mismatches.suggested_fix: 30,000 inbound applications produced one design hire, so ElevenLabs went out and found people: its design team grew from 8 to 35 in a year and 60% of those hires were sourced. Try the lookalike search: give an AI model 50 people you rate and ask it for similar ones.

mismatches.digest_line: Ava Labs publishes a 'never list' so candidates can spot impostors: its recruiters will never ask a candidate to install software or to run code on their own computer.
mismatches.source_says: Transcript [52:33] to [53:35], Luke Eaton: "I can walk you through roughly kind of what we're doing ... on our job board, um, and then we're we're getting the marketing team to sort of make our careers page a bit more focused around it as well" ... "So publishing your hiring stack around there. Um, I I call it a never list ... So we will never ask you to install software. We will never ask you to run a repo locally. ... this is something that's you know trained into all of our team". He describes work in progress and gives it as advice; he never says Ava Labs has published the never list. Borderline, but 'publishes' as a settled fact is not stated.
mismatches.suggested_fix: Luke Eaton of Ava Labs says to publish a 'never list' so candidates can spot impostors, such as: we will never ask you to install software or to run a code project on your own machine.

mismatches.digest_line: Zapier is fully remote with just under 1,000 people in 42 countries, yet it no longer hires from anywhere, judging some countries better than others on labour law and tax.
mismatches.source_says: Transcript [14:58] and the paragraph before: "even at Zapier, we used to say we hire from anywhere, and now as I mentioned before, we're saying, oh, but maybe like these places are better than these places because some of the labor laws or tax requirements or the accommodations that we have to make are actually like so much work". The source says Zapier has stopped SAYING it hires from anywhere and now weighs countries; it does not state a policy that it no longer hires from anywhere. Borderline tightening.
mismatches.suggested_fix: Zapier is fully remote with just under 1,000 people in 42 countries, yet it has stopped saying it hires from anywhere and now rates some countries above others on labour law and tax.
